dialogue.Introduction: Eh? A new face in the saloon. I'm the Tavernkeep, and this is the only bar between the desert and the mountains that still has a roof.#$b#Sit where you like, but the stool by the piano is cursed. Don't ask.$h
dialogue.Mon: Monday. Every Monday is the same. The Merchant haggles my prices and the Nurse orders a stiff drink, then yells at me for pouring it.$h
dialogue.Tue: Another day, another keg of cider that tastes like the cellar. Could you carry a crate for me, @? You look like you would drop it.$a
dialogue.Wed: Wednesday. Half the valley is out in the fields and the other half is in here complaining about the fields.$h
dialogue.Thu: The Painter came in yesterday and tried to pay in sketches. I took the sketches. They are wrapped around my bottles now.$u
dialogue.Fri: Friday night is the busiest night. You would think the mines would give everyone a rest, but the miners just get thirstier.$h
dialogue.Sat: Saturday, and I have not had a moment to sit down. The Demolitionist wants to know if I have spare gunpowder. The answer is no.$a
dialogue.Sun: Sundays are slow. The valley takes a breath, the Dryad goes off to talk to her trees, and I get to wipe the same counter again.$s
dialogue.Mon2: Eh. You again, @? Fine, pull up a stool. The stool does not care who sits on it.$h
dialogue.Tue2: Tuesday already. The Angler spilled her drink on my floor again, so mind the sticky patch by the door.$h
dialogue.Wed2: I keep a bottle of Ale for everyone who gets through a Wednesday in this town. You are still standing, so you qualify.$h
dialogue.Thu2: The Mechanic fixed the tap line again. It works now, mostly. Try not to lean on it.$h
dialogue.Fri2: Friday again, and the piano is still floating in the corner. Nobody has asked me to explain it, so I am not going to.$u
dialogue.Sat2: Saturday is the day the regulars tell their tallest stories. Keep your ears open, @, some of them are even true.$h
dialogue.Sun2: Fancy seeing you on a slow Sunday. Careful, the floor sticks. I am still trying to figure out why.$h
dialogue.Mon4: Ah, @, Mondays are better with you in them. Don't tell the Merchant I said so, he will raise the price of my company.$h
dialogue.Tue4: Tuesday and you are still here. I would call you a regular now, though I won't let you sit where the Angler spills her drinks.$h
dialogue.Wed4: The Stylist asked me for a haircut recommendation. I told her the only cut I know is the one from the bar fight last week.$h
dialogue.Thu4: You know this valley better than most now. Tell me what you have seen out there, I only ever hear it second hand.$h
dialogue.Fri4: Friday is my favourite, @. The saloon is full of people I would not trade for any kingdom. Including you, even when you track mud across my floor.$h
dialogue.Sat4: If the Party Girl throws another party in my saloon, she pays for the broken glass. That is the deal. She has not agreed yet, but I am working on her.$h
dialogue.Sun4: I used to pour for a whole kingdom, you know. Now it is a dozen people and a dog who sleeps under the piano. Better, honestly. Quieter.$h
dialogue.Mon6: Careful, @. If you keep coming in this often, I will have to start remembering your order.$h
dialogue.Tue6: Someone spilled a potion on the piano and now it floats. I am not going to ask who. I am going to let it float.$u
dialogue.Thu6: The Dye Trader came in with a bucket of color and asked me to be his model. I said no. He asked again. I am still saying no.$a
dialogue.Sat6: You have been a fine customer, @. Good tips, quiet manners, and you never set off explosions in the back room. I would call that a friend.$h
dialogue.Mon8: Between us? I am glad you came to town, @. I was starting to think this place would never fill up again.#$b#Don't tell anybody that, I have a reputation to keep.$l
dialogue.Tue8: Some nights I stand back here and count the regulars and worry. One of them will get hurt in the mines, one will get lonely. I never say anything, but I count.$s
dialogue.Wed8: You can talk to me, you know. Anything. I am no healer, but I am a good listener. The Nurse says so, and she never compliments anyone.$h
dialogue.Thu8: My old tavern in Eternia had a window that looked out on the sea. I never could fix the glass after the storms. Here the valley is calm enough that I might finally do it.$s
dialogue.Fri8: @, when I see you come through that door my whole day gets better. I do not say it much, but it is true.$l
dialogue.Sat8: There is a lot of history behind this bar. The Clothier's cursed past, the Wizard's bad ideas, the Princess's royal tab. I am glad to have someone new to share the stories with.$h
dialogue.Sun8: I keep thinking about what I will do when the hard times come. I will pour drinks, that is what. Drinks help people face anything.$h
dialogue.Mon10: I have been thinking, @. You can come in any time, even after closing. The door is never locked for you.$h
dialogue.Sun10: I have decided. If I ever had one last bottle to share, you would be the one I shared it with. Don't make me regret saying that.$h
dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer Wednesdays are hot enough to melt the bottles. I keep the cellar cold, so come down and cool off.$h
dialogue.summer_Sat: The Luau is coming, and the soup had better not be cooked by the Dryad again. Last year it tasted like a tree.$a
dialogue.fall_Fri: Fall nights are my favourite. The mines are quiet, the stars are out, and the regulars come in with stories.$h
dialogue.winter_Tue: Brr. The cold pushes everyone into the saloon. My fireplace has never been so popular, or so messy.$s
dialogue.spring_Thu: Spring means the Painter starts trying to paint my bar. I told her the bar is already a masterpiece of spilled drinks.$h
dialogue.winter_Fri8: Cold night, warm drink. There is nothing more I would want from this town, @.$l
dialogue.fall_15: Half of fall is gone already. The leaves blow in through the door and I have to sweep them out every hour.$s
dialogue.spring_7: Oh, look at the spring flowers. The Dryad would be proud. I will put a few on the bar. Don't ask me where I got them.$h
dialogue.winter_12: The Festival of Ice is coming and I am not chopping any more ice for the fishing contest. The Angler can do it herself.$a
dialogue.fall_28: The last days of fall. Winter is coming, and so is the Festival of Ice. I am already stocking the cellar with extra Ale.$h

rainy: Rain again. The roof leaks right over the piano, so the piano is getting a bath. Come in before you get soaked, @.$h

situations.eye: The Eye is gone? Well, my windows are safe for another night. Drinks are on me this round.$h
situations.evilBoss: Something nasty from the caves was finally put down, and the whole valley heard it. Good riddance. My cellar is safe now.$h
situations.skeletron: The dungeon is open and the Old Man is free, so the Clothier has been telling his cursed past story at full volume. I would rather have quiet.$a
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is down. Honey is cheap at the Merchant's now, and I am stocking the mead. Don't say I never think of you.$h
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh fell and hardmode began. Every monster out there got tougher, and every drink in here got more expensive. My prices, not theirs.$u
situations.mechs: One of the mechanical bosses was smashed to bits last night. The noise rattled every bottle on my shelf. I am charging extra for the broken glass.$a
situations.plantera: Plantera is gone, and the jungle temple is open. Somebody will come in here bragging about it by noon, and I am ready to listen.$h
situations.golem: The Golem is finally down. I heard the crash from the saloon. The stone creature was rude, but its loot is worth the trouble.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist fell last night, and the celestial pillars are out there glowing. Stay away from them, friend, and drink some water.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is defeated. Everyone is hoarse from cheering, and I poured free drinks until the kegs ran dry. Worth it.$h
situations.goblins: The goblin army got sent packing. Their tinkerers keep trying to sell me junk now. I told the Goblin Tinkerer to stay out of my bar.$a
situations.pirates: The pirates were driven back into the sea. Their captain left a tab. I expect the Pirate will pay it, one way or another.$a
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion is gone. Those snowmen did not even stop for a drink first, rude creatures. The cold is still sitting on my doorstep.$s
situations.martians: A Martian Madness was repelled last night. Their ships are all over the sky. I told them the saloon was closed, and they did not believe me.$u
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night, and the zombies came up through the dirt pounding on my doors. I have boarded up the front, friend. Drink up before dark.$s
situations.eclipse: The eclipse turned the whole valley dark at noon. I could not see the bottles at all, so I poured by feel. If the drink tastes odd, that is why.$u
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today, in my saloon, without asking me first. She promised to pay for the glass. I am not holding my breath.$a

festivals.spring13: The Egg Festival is the one day I close early. Nobody brings an egg to the saloon anymore, so I bring a bottle instead.$h
festivals.spring24: A Flower Dance without a barkeep is no dance at all. I will be here at the bar, dancing with my bottles.$h
festivals.summer11: The Luau soup is in the pot. Somebody put mead in it. Please don't tell the Dryad, she would be furious and I would be buying the next round.$h
festivals.summer28: The jellies glow on the beach tonight. I usually watch from the saloon porch, but tonight I will walk down with you, @.$h
festivals.fall16: The grange displays are fine. My ale won the blue ribbon for the third year running, and nobody has proven it is not a family recipe.$h
festivals.fall27: The haunted maze is full of spooks, and the saloon is full of drunk spooks. Stay close, and do not follow any lantern that laughs at you.$u
festivals.winter8: The ice fishing contest is my favourite. The Angler is out there with her sad little rod, so I am backing her with a hot cocoa.$h
festivals.winter25: I got a bottle from the secret gift exchange. I will keep the label a secret too, until you tell me what you got.$h

loved.text: Now that is a drink worth pouring. Thank you, friend, you know my weakness.$h

liked.text: Hah, that is a fine addition to the shelf. Thanks, @.$h

neutral.text: Hm. Thanks, I will put it behind the bar.

disliked.text: Ugh, you could have brought a cork instead. Thanks, I think.$a

hated.text: Get that out of my tavern before the Demolitionist sees it.$a

help: Bit of help here? I am not paid enough for this!
Last call for whatever is biting me! Help!
Hey! Somebody stop this one before the glass breaks!
thanks: Eh, thanks, @. That one was going to wreck my cellar.$h
Hah, you saved my bar, @. Drinks are on me next time.$h
battle: Last call for you, you overgrown rat!
Get out of my tavern, you big ugly thing!
Free drinks to whoever ends this. Come on!
courage.hurt: Ow. Something took a bite out of me, and I am not going back out there tonight. Sit, @, and keep the stool warm.$s

danger.boss: A big nasty is loose out there and it is headed for the valley. Bar is closing early. Grab a weapon, @.$a
danger.invasion: The invaders are at the gates. Good, I have been wanting an excuse to swing this bar stool at something.$h
danger.pumpkinMoon: Pumpkin moon is up. Scarecrows are walking and the pumpkin folk are howling. Keep your lantern lit, @.$h
danger.frostMoon: Frost moon, and the cold is coming down the hill. Bring a warm drink and a sharp blade, friend.$h
danger.eclipse: The sky went dark and the monsters came out with it. I am bolting the door, and then I am going out, @.$u
danger.bloodMoon: Blood moon. Zombies are pounding on my boards. Good. I have been itching for a fight all week.$h

events.after: Still slow in here, but I'm glad you stopped by.

steps.say: Oh! @, you startled me. I was wiping the same spot for the fifth time. Nobody has come in all morning.$u
Sit down, sit down. Business is slow and the Tavernkeep is bored. Bored is dangerous behind a bar.#$b#Don't mind me, I am just talking to the wood again.$h

answers.reply: Then you came to the right counter. Sit, and I will pour.$h
Looking, is it? Buy something or I will start charging for the stools.$a

steps.say: On the house today, since you are the only customer. Fruit juice, not that swill from the cellar.$h

events.after: Pop in again, the stools are always warm for you.

steps.say: Oh, @, you are just in time. Pull up a stool and keep your hands where I can see them.$h
Relax, barkeep. The keg only got a little warm, and nobody got hurt.$h
A little warm? It is singing, friend. Singing kegs do not stay on my counter.$a

answers.reply: Good, the lecture is free and nobody wants it.$h
Brave. Sit down, and both are on the house.$h

steps.say: Between you and me, this is the best part of my day. The regulars are trouble, but they are my trouble.#$b#I would miss the noise if it stopped.$h
Here, a fresh pour. Don't spill it on the piano. It has already floated once this week.$u

events.after: Still got the taste of the sea in my mouth, @.

steps.say: Shh. Listen to that. The waves do not ask for a tab.$h
I used to walk a shore like this one, back home in Eternia. The kingdom had a sea, and I had a whole road of inns.#$b#Some nights I still hear the gulls and think it is the old harbor.$s

answers.reply: Hah. You are a good listener, @. Terrible for business, but good.$h

answers.text: Not really, this valley is nicer.
answers.reply: Nicer, aye. Quieter too. Nobody here has tried to start a war over my tavern.$h

steps.say: Here, take this Ale. It is the good stuff, saved for a night like this one.$h
Don't tell the Merchant what it cost. He will want a cut of the sunset.$h

events.after: I still count the regulars, but you are the one I count first.

steps.say: Closing time already? Hm. Sit a minute, @. You are not a customer any more.$h

I have poured for everyone who walked into this town. The Nurse with her sarcasm, the Merchant with his prices, the Golfer ruining my floor.#$b#Hah. But I never asked any of them how they were holding up.$s

steps.question: How are you holding up, Tavernkeep?

answers.reply: Then go home and sleep. The chairs will still be here tomorrow.$h
Fair enough. But the offer stays open. It always does.$h

steps.say: Here, I keep a bottle of the old Eternian stuff under the counter for emergencies. This one is for you.$h
Don't tell the others I gave you the good bottle.$l

events.after: Keep that sunny weather coming, my back is tired of cellar air.

steps.say: Look at this, @. Sunlight. A whole field of it, and nobody is shouting for a refill.$h
Don't laugh. I have been stuck behind a counter for years, and I wanted to see what the valley looks like when nobody is buying.#$b#Turns out it looks a lot like home, minus the cliffs.$s

steps.question: Glad you came out here with me?

answers.reply: Hah. Stop it, you will make me cry into my own bottles.$l
A little is more than I expected from you, @.$h

steps.say: When I first got here I thought I would hate it. Now I would miss this valley if it moved away.$h
Do me a favour and keep that sunny weather coming. My back is tired of cellar air.$h
